concepts.title: Understanding Acids, Bases and Their Chemical Properties

questions.q: State three chemical properties of acids.
questions.a: Acids turn blue litmus red, react with metals giving hydrogen, and with carbonates giving CO2.

questions.q: What is common in all acids that makes them behave alike?
questions.a: In water all acids release hydrogen ions (hydronium ions).

questions.q: Why is lime water used to test acids of carbonates?
questions.a: The CO2 released turns lime water milky, confirming the acid-carbonate reaction.

questions.q: What does the pH of a solution tell us?
questions.a: It tells how acidic or basic a solution is: pH under 7 acidic, 7 neutral, above 7 basic.

questions.q: Which has a lower pH, lemon juice or soap solution?
questions.a: Lemon juice (acidic, pH about 2) has much lower pH than a soap solution (basic, pH about 9-10).

questions.q: Why must an antacid be taken for acidity?
questions.a: It neutralises excess stomach acid, relieving the burning pain of indigestion.
Salts sharing the same positive or negative radical belong to one family, e.g. sodium chloride and sodium sulphate are sodium salts.

questions.q: Name the salt used in baking and state why cakes rise.
questions.a: Baking soda (sodium hydrogencarbonate) releases CO2 on heating, puffing up the cake.
